parsed.title: Expats and job hunting in Slovakia and Austria

claims.text: Some participants know individuals living abroad, including one in Austria and one in Poland.
Participant P3 has at least two acquaintances in Austria, one recently arrived and another who has been there for several years.
LinkedIn is recommended as the primary tool for finding jobs abroad.
A high volume of applications (about 100) typically yields only a few interview invitations (3).
Most job postings in the region require knowledge of the local language.
German is the main spoken language in Austria, though English is also used.
Employers commonly ask for a B2 level of the local language, with B1 sometimes accepted; certificates are rarely required.
Workplace communication can be conducted in English.
Conversion from applications to interviews is low, e.g., 3 interviews from ~100 applications.
Candidates with 2–3 years of experience can secure interviews even without strong language skills.
Salaries in Europe are generally higher than in Ukraine, though many overlook this factor.
Even the minimal accepted salary was still higher than fast‑food wages.
Learning the local language is important for daily life and feeling comfortable in the city.
Typical employer requirement is B2, but B1 may be sufficient; candidates often list B2 in resumes without certification.

decisions.text: Use LinkedIn as the primary platform for searching jobs abroad.
